gateOrderingProof.description: Confirmed by inspection (not just trusting labels) that scripts/verify-v9-closure.mjs performs, strictly in order: (1) require OMNIA_V9_TEST_DATABASE_URL or exit 2, (2) spawn npm run test:v9 and exit non-zero on failure, (3) print OMNIA_V9_REAL_POSTGRES_FULL_SUITE_VERIFIED only after that succeeds, (4) spawn scripts/verify-v9-p3.mjs and require status === 'P3_POLICY_VERIFIED', (5) print OMNIA_V9_CEDAR_POLICY_VERIFIED only after that succeeds, (6) spawn 'node --test tests/omnia-v9-end-to-end-proof-circuit.test.mjs' and exit non-zero on failure, (7) print OMNIA_V9_CLOSURE_CIRCUIT_VERIFIED only after that succeeds, (8) print OMNIA_V9_CLOSURE_VERIFIED last. No success marker is printed before its corresponding gate's spawnSync call returns success.

migrationTrackingDefectFound.description: Migrations 005-008 never registered themselves in the schema_migrations ledger, unlike 001-004. Reproduced: ran scripts/migrate.mjs against a genuinely empty database and found only 001-004 recorded in schema_migrations despite all 30 tables (including all 7 omnia_v9_* tables) existing. This meant scripts/migrate.mjs would silently re-run all four V9 migration files' full DDL on every single invocation forever, and schema_migrations would permanently misreport that V9 was never migrated in.
migrationTrackingDefectFound.fixDetail: each of 005-008 now runs CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS schema_migrations(...) followed by INSERT ... ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING for its own version string, matching the 001-004 pattern. The CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS guard (not a bare INSERT) is required because these four files are also applied standalone by most V9 test fixtures (PGlite instances, ad hoc real-Postgres pools) that never run the full app bootstrap — a naive bare-INSERT version broke 20 of 23 tests in tests/omnia-v9-proof-store.test.mjs with 'relation schema_migrations does not exist' before this guard was added; this was caught and corrected within this same pass.
migrationTrackingDefectFound.verifiedAfterFix: fresh database + scripts/migrate.mjs now registers all 8 migration versions in schema_migrations; scripts/migrate.mjs is idempotent on rerun (second invocation touches nothing); all V9 standalone test fixtures still pass

mutationTestResultsCaveat: Time-boxed to the protections explicitly named across both closure missions. Not attempted: a live DROP CONSTRAINT on the omnia_v9_execution_receipt_bindings unique/PK constraints themselves (as opposed to the application-level conflict-detection logic that sits in front of them), because that table has FK-dependent tables (omnia_v9_execution_authorization_bindings) and a cascading drop was judged too risky on a shared disposable database for the value gained — the application-level check that sits in front of the constraint was mutated and caught instead, and the constraint's own behavior is exercised structurally by every real-Postgres concurrency race passing.
